articles.title: J&K industry pins hopes on new policy push
articles.description: Srinagar, Oct 23: Industrial entrepreneurs across Jammu and Kashmir see Chief Minister Omar Abdullah-led government’s proposed New Industrial Policy as a potential turning point for a sector grappling with financial distress, limited market access, regulatory hurdles, and years of accumulated liabilities. With the policy nearing finalisation, industry representatives hope the framework will address the difficulties confronting existing enterprises while creating a more predictable environment for fresh investments, technological modernisation and employment generation. Expectations have gathered momentum following Chief Minister Omar Abdullah’s assurance that the final draft would be shared with representative industry bodies for their suggestions before its unveiling. The proposed policy follows sustained demands from industrial stakeholders for a framework that reflects Jammu and Kashmir’s specific economic challenges. Business chambers have argued that existing arrangements have not adequately addressed the financial and operational difficulties faced by local manufacturing units, particularly enterprises affected by prolonged disruptions and accumulated debt. Responding to these concerns, the government initiated consultations with industry representatives and constituted a three-member drafting committee under Additional Chief Secretary, Finance, Shailender Kumar. Commissioner Secretary, Industries and Commerce, Vikramjeet Singh, and J&K Bank Managing Director and CEO Amitava Chatterjee are its other members. The Federation of Chambers of Industries Kashmir (FCIK), the Kashmir Chamber of Industries and Commerce and other business organisations have held discussions with the government and submitted representations outlining their priorities. Their principal demands include improvements in Ease of Doing Business, preferential public procurement for local manufacturers, rehabilitation of sick industrial units, uniform fiscal and non-fiscal incentives, infrastructure development, technological upgradation and institutional reforms. Investment decisions await policy clarity Several industrial entrepreneurs are awaiting clarity on the proposed framework before committing fresh capital to expansion, modernisation and diversification. Industry representatives say a credible policy could encourage existing units to restore idle capacity, adopt modern production technologies and explore new markets. A key development in this direction has been the enactment of the Jammu and Kashmir Ease of Doing Business Act, 2026. The legislation is intended to simplify regulatory procedures, eliminate redundant clearances and reduce administrative discretion. Industrial chambers have welcomed the move towards a more facilitative regulatory environment but are awaiting notification of the rules and operational guidelines. They maintain that implementation will be critical, with procedures that are straightforward, transparent and supported by time-bound decisions. Industry representatives argue that the proposed Industrial Policy must complement the legislation by addressing constraints that extend beyond administrative approvals, including access to finance, infrastructure, market opportunities and the revival of financially stressed businesses. Local manufacturers seek procurement preference Preferential public procurement remains one of the industry’s principal demands. Manufacturers contend that local enterprises with available production capacity often struggle to secure government orders because of tender conditions and procurement arrangements that favour larger suppliers or companies operating outside the region. Industry bodies have sought a clearly defined preference for locally manufactured products, rationalisation of tender conditions, wider participation by micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and timely payment of government dues. They argue that a transparent procurement framework could help local manufacturers achieve economies of scale, improve capacity utilisation and generate employment while retaining a greater share of public expenditure within Jammu and Kashmir. Revival of sick units and settlement of legacy liabilities A comprehensive rehabilitation framework for sick and financially stressed industrial units is another major expectation. Industry representatives maintain that prolonged disruptions, erosion of working capital and mounting financial liabilities have pushed several otherwise viable enterprises into distress. They want the new policy to provide a structured route for rehabilitation through financial restructuring, restoration of working capital and appropriate relief on accumulated government dues. Their demands include consideration of relief or settlement mechanisms for electricity arrears, industrial estate ground rent and other statutory liabilities, subject to applicable rules and eligibility criteria. The objective, they say, should be to help viable enterprises resume operations rather than leave them trapped in a cycle of mounting dues, restricted credit and declining production. J&K Bank OTS scheme remains crucial Closely linked to industrial revival is the proposed One Time Settlement (OTS) scheme from Jammu and Kashmir Bank. Industry representatives say the bank’s management had assured them that an OTS initiative would be introduced in conjunction with the New Industrial Policy. They have sought a settlement framework comparable to the State Bank of India’s OTS-20 scheme, particularly its coverage of eligible stressed accounts up to Rs 50 crore. The chambers are pressing for transparent, predictable and non-discriminatory eligibility criteria and meaningful settlement concessions for borrowers affected by prolonged economic disruptions. They argue that a workable OTS mechanism, combined with restructuring and access to fresh institutional credit, could help eligible businesses settle legacy banking stress and return to productive activity. The final terms, eligibility conditions and implementation timeline of any J&K Bank scheme, however, remain matters for the bank to formally establish. A test of industrial revival Industry representatives believe the New Industrial Policy must bring together regulatory reform, financial rehabilitation, infrastructure development and market access within a coherent framework. They have welcomed the government’s consultative approach and its stated willingness to address the concerns of existing enterprises while encouraging new investment. The stakes extend beyond individual businesses. A stronger industrial base could expand employment opportunities for educated and skilled youth, deepen local supply chains, support entrepreneurship and reduce the need for young people to leave the region in search of work. For entrepreneurs who have endured years of financial and operational challenges, the forthcoming policy represents an opportunity to resolve legacy problems and plan for future growth with greater confidence. With the Ease of Doing Business Act enacted and the Industrial Policy approaching finalisation, industry stakeholders are looking to Chief Minister Omar Abdullah-led government to translate its reform agenda into clear, time-bound and implementable measures. Whether the new framework delivers a genuine industrial revival will ultimately depend on its provisions, implementation and the extent to which long-pending demands translate into tangible relief and new economic opportunities.

articles.title: Maharashtra Fast-Tracks Long-Awaited Purandar Greenfield Airport; MADC Invites Bids For Master Plan & PPP Concessionaire Selection
articles.description: Maharashtra Airport Development Company has floated a tender for an eight-month techno-economic feasibility study of Pune's proposed Purandar International Airport. The consultant will prepare a master plan, assess airspace compatibility, develop traffic forecasts until 2070-71 and support PPP concessionaire selection.

articles.title: TheTenders Offers Comprehensive Tender Bidding Support and GeM Portal Services to Help Businesses Access Government Opportunities
articles.description: New Delhi [India], October 23: The Government e-Marketplace (GeM) is an online public procurement platform that enables eligible sellers, manufacturers, contractors, and service providers to offer goods and services to government departments and other authorised buyers. Businesses can explore GeM Tenders in India and participate in procurement opportunities according to the applicable eligibility criteria, tender conditions, and platform policies.
